newsitem.title: UK: PRESS DIGEST - London Evening Standard - Dec 18.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - London Evening Standard - Dec 18.

text.p: Prepared for Reuters by The Broadcast Monitoring Company
THE ROAD TO SILENT NIGHTS IN LONDON

Millions across the UK suffer sleepless nights due to continuous traffic noise. The RAC claimed that such pollution could be cut by 85 percent through the use of porous asphalt. However penny pinching road maintenance budgets ruled this solution out.
SOCIETIES BILL LIFTS THREATS TO PAY OUTS

The Building Societies Bill is set to retain converting societies' protection from take over. Societies led by the Alliance & Leicester had threatened to halt flotation if the cover was abandoned. Protection was seen as vital for the retention of independence against stiff competition.
SIB PROMPTS METAL MARKET SHAKE UP TALKS

The London Metal Exchange planned to reform the market's regulatory structure following the SIB's report on the Hamanaka copper scandal. The SIB proposed cutting the number of member firm-nominated directors on the LME's board. A source claimed , "The Exchange's executive was determined to reduce the power of member firms."

The pound was on the up as British retail sales were expected to remain buoyant. November retail sales were predicted to be 0.4% up on October with a year on year rise of 3.2%. Foreign exchange traders believed there would be a rise in rates sooner rather than later.
